title: SPECTRA: State-Space Exogenous Context and Temporal-Frequency Resolution Architecture for Probabilistic Energy Forecasting
note: arXiv record, v1 only, 22 Jul 2026, stat.ML; 10 pages, said to be submitted to IEEE Trans. Power Systems. Abstract: a trained architecture that splits the series into a deterministic and a residual stream and aligns exogenous inputs with both; best CRPS in 14 of 18 load, price, solar and wind settings, average CRPS 5.74% and upper-tail quantile risk 7.27% below the strongest baselines.

title: SPECTRA (full text, v1)
note: Data: ECL (321 clients, hourly, 2012-2014); Open Power System Data 2015-2017 (59 load, 31 price, 36 solar, 57 wind series); GEFCom2014 load and price 2011-2014 with temperature, calendar, holiday covariates, solar and wind 2012-2013 with weather. Chronological 7:1:2 split, so the test part is the last 20%; no dates or origin counts given. Input 168 h; training-set normalisation.

title: SPECTRA (full text, v1)
note: Table I: 9 dataset-task pairs x 2 horizon groups = 18 settings. Short = mean over 12, 24, 36 steps; long = mean over 72, 120, 168 (solar and wind: 72 only). 168 h is never reported on its own. CRPS is a normalised quantile-score approximation over 99 quantiles. Text: best CRPS in 14 of 18, top two in 17; average gain 5.74% CRPS, 7.27% rho90, 1.78% rho50 (median error).

title: SPECTRA (full text, v1)
note: Table I load cells, CRPS, SPECTRA vs best baseline (short / long): ECL 0.150 vs TADNet 0.169 / 0.187 vs 0.197; OPS load 0.107 vs TADNet 0.134 / 0.162 vs 0.184; GEFCom2014 load 0.166 vs TFT 0.172 / 0.253 vs TimeXer 0.254 (TADNet 0.255). It loses on OPS price long and OPS wind (PatchTST, DLinear) and ties TFT on GEF wind short. No intervals or deviations in the table.

title: SPECTRA (full text, v1)
note: Baselines: DeepAR, TFT, TADNet, TiDE, TimeXer, Autoformer, PatchTST, DLinear, all trained by the authors with the same split, horizons, quantile set and pinball loss; point models got a quantile head. The paper does not say which baselines received the exogenous inputs. No statistical or naive baseline, no regression on temperature, no pretrained model. Means of 3 seeds; one NVIDIA A30 GPU.

title: yedadasd/SPECTRA: official implementation
note: Authors' repository, linked from the paper. 14 commits, oldest shown 19 Apr 2026, head 7b220ab of 28 Jul 2026. PyTorch model code, loaders, preprocessing and per-dataset scripts for SPECTRA and the baselines. No licence file in the listing, no releases, no tags, no trained weights (checkpoints are written locally by training). README repeats 14/18, 17/18, 5.74% and 7.27%. 1 star, 0 forks.

title: yedadasd/SPECTRA: official implementation
note: Setup: Python 3.10, needs mamba-ssm and pytorch-wavelets; a CUDA GPU is recommended. Scripts expect preprocessed CSVs under ./dataset/ which are not in the repository listing, and no download links are given. The README's example command trains with three quantiles (0.1, 0.5, 0.9), while the paper evaluates 99; whether the paper's scripts differ was not checked. No dependency pins.

title: SPECTRA (full text, v1)
note: Inputs: the exogenous series spans history plus the whole horizon (L+H), so covariates enter as known into the future. Only the separate NewEnergy2025 case study (15-minute solar and wind, 96 steps) names meteorological forecasts. Robustness to imperfect exogenous inputs is left as future work. Ablation without the exogenous module: CRPS +4.5% on ECL, +9.3% on OPS load.

title: SPECTRA/data_provider
note: Directory listing only: a data factory, a loader and preprocessing scripts for GEFCom2014, Open Power System Data, solar and the NewEnergy power set; last changed 24 Jul 2026. The file contents were not opened, so how future covariates are built for the baselines is not verified.

title: SPECTRA_GEFCom2014_all.sh
note: A five-line wrapper that calls the four GEFCom2014 task scripts (load, price, solar, wind). It holds no settings itself; the load script was not opened.

title: SPECTRA: Pith review page
note: Not fetched; from the research tool's sources. An automated review of the paper, not a rerun. It describes the architecture as new and, per the research answer, points to near-ties in the table, three seeds without error bars and undisclosed spectral and loss hyperparameters. Secondary: used as a lead only, not cited.

title: search: SPECTRA State-Space Exogenous Context replication or comparison
note: One search (LinkedIn excluded) and one standard research task found no independent replication, critique with new numbers, pre-registration, released weights or Hugging Face model. Results were the paper's own pages, the automated review page and unrelated ResearchGate pages. The research answer said the horizon groups were not readable; the fetched full text gives them.
